summary: Walter Slaje is an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna from circa 1974 to 1979. He held a post as Prof. Dr at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1999 to 2020.

Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz was a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at Stanford University, studied at the University of Oxford and Jesus College, and studied under traditional teacher Kazi Dawa Samdup.

Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied under Ernst Leumann from circa 1900 to 1904. He served as a professor at the University of Hamburg (attested 1958) and taught Seiren Matsunami, Ludwig Alsdorf, and Frank-Richard Hamm.

Walther Wüst was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from circa 1919 to 1923 and later served as its rector from 1941 to 1946.

Wang Pachow was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology who studied under Yun-shan Tan. He served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University and taught Dale S. Wright.

Wannaporn Rienjang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology who earned a PhD at the University of Cambridge. Her posts include roles at the British Museum, the University of Oxford, and Thammasat University.
Warren Cowgill was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Stanford University (circa 1948–1952) and Yale University (circa 1952–1957), where he held a post in 1956.

Warren Lee Todd is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who completed his PhD at Lancaster University, supervised by Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad (attested 2012). He also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Peter Harvey, and traditional teacher Chogye Trichen Rinpoche.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University. His MA was supervised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, and he also studied under Phra Sudhivorayan and Phramaha Somjin Sammāpañño.

Wasu Harada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Ryukoku and Koyasan universities. He held academic posts at Koyasan University, Ryukoku University, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, and Shuchiin University.

Wataru S. Ryose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 1987 under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota, and also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances A. Wilson.

Wayne Proudfoot is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Harvard Divinity School (circa 1961–1964) and Harvard University (circa 1964–1972), and held a post at Columbia University from circa 1972 to 2017.

Wei Lin is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD from Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. Lin held posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum, Western Michigan University, University of Michigan, and Transylvania University.

Wei-jen Teng is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Chicago and earned a PhD at Harvard University. He has held a teaching post at the Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.
Weirong Shen is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held posts as a teacher at the University of Hong Kong and at Renmin University of China from circa 2006 to 2017.
Weiru Guan is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2011) under the supervision of Yongdong Shi.
Wen-ling Jane is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned a PhD at Columbia University, where she was supervised by Robert A. F. Thurman and also studied under Lobsang Jamspal.

Wenbiao Mai is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Kyoto University, the University of Hamburg, and earned a PhD at Peking University. Mai held a post at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Wendi L. Adamek is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who earned a PhD at Stanford University. She held posts at Barnard College (attested 2008) and as an associate professor at the University of Calgary (attested 2018).

Wendy Doniger is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Radcliffe College, Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and the University of Oxford. She held a long-term professorship at the University of Chicago.
